Senses.PreferredTarget: turn the light around and shine back
AlternateTargets: turn the light back and illuminate
turn illumination around and shine back
Senses.Explanation: Literally, 'turn the light around and shine back': 'turn around' (迴), 'light' (光), 'return' (返), and 'shine or illuminate' (照). This written form occurs 50 times in 35 allowed texts; the common variant 'turn the light around and shine back' (回光返照) occurs 168 times in 88 texts, and the reversed order 'shine back and turn the light' (返照回光) occurs 16 times. The Record of the Transmission of the Lamp gives the literal instruction, 'turn the light around and shine back; look: what are body and mind?' (迴光返照看身心是何物). Shitou's Grass Hut Song says, 'turn the light around and shine back, then return' (迴光返照便歸來). Linji tells his listeners that at the words they should 'themselves turn the light around and shine back, seeking nothing else' (便自迴光返照，更不別求). Chengtian Cique says, 'only turn the light around and shine back; carefully search beneath your own heels and look what it is' (但自迴光返照，向自己脚根下子細推尋，看是箇什麼). Gongchen Jueke closes an address with 'each of you, please turn the light around and shine back; do not hesitate further' (各請迴光返照，休更踟躕). Fenyang's verse supplies a result-clause: 'turn the light around and shine back, illuminating present and past' (迴光返照明今古). The corpus thus records an imperative verb phrase, a poetic return, a prohibition on seeking elsewhere, and direct objects or complements such as body and mind, beneath one's heels, and present and past.
Senses.Note: No required direct-definition formula was found. The entry translates the four graphs and the actions explicitly attached to them. It does not rename those instructions as a special exercise or import an external system. The common orthographic variant is recorded in the explanation, while the assigned headword and all curated anchors retain the assigned written form.
